_readme: Projects shown on lorcan.space/websites, in order. To add one: capture screenshots into img/web/ (see build_websites.py), add an entry here, then run build_websites.py and build.mjs. layout: one of split, stage, mirror, cinema.

projects.name: O'Neill Construction
projects.summary: A website for an Irish construction group working across commercial, residential, industrial and civil projects.

projects.name: Brandit
projects.label: Website concept
projects.summary: A campaign-style home page and an enquiry-only shop for a Dublin promotional products company.
projects.thinking: Built to sell without a checkout: browse the range, add items to an enquiry list and ask for a quote with a mock-up of your logo. Bright, product-first and quick to scan.

details.cap: Range at a glance: six categories, one tap each
The enquiry flow, explained in three steps

projects.name: Whitestone
projects.label: Website concept
projects.summary: A premium landing page for a specialist fabric-care service in the UAE.
projects.thinking: Editorial serif typography, arched imagery and a muted olive palette, paced like a magazine. The page had to feel as considered as the fabrics the business looks after.

details.cap: Care is in the details: the philosophy section
The process, set in deep olive

projects.name: Hymonic
projects.label: Prototype
projects.summary: A product website for modular ammonia cracking that delivers hydrogen on site.
projects.thinking: Dense engineering made readable. The reaction, the output range and the system profile each sit in one card, so a buyer understands the technology before reading a paragraph.

details.cap: The containerised system, with the numbers that matter beside it

projects.name: Flying Fish
projects.label: Independent redesign concept
projects.built: Hand-built HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with a Three.js 3D model
projects.summary: An independent take on the website of a Delft company building hydrofoil systems and water mobility software.
projects.thinking: Dark, cinematic and full-bleed, with an interactive 3D vessel that shows how a boat lifts onto its foils. The projects read like case studies, not a logo wall.

details.cap: Hydrofoil systems, introduced with a concept render
Projects presented as stories, each with its key figure
